newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs firm again on selective buys.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs firm again on selective buys.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) posted mild gains on Thursday as selective demand appeared in a quiet market, traders said.
They said activity was seen limited in the short term as the market absorbed a planned GDR issue by telecoms group VSNL.

"The market will be quiet until the VSNL issue, with selling possible in some stocks to make way for VSNL," a trader said, adding that new investment was also expected in the issue as it was the first Indian telecoms stock in the GDR market.
Pricing and allocation for the issue is expected on March 24.
The trader said gains on the day had been driven by fresh investment in selected stocks, and the market overall was mixed.
Hindalco collected 75 cents to $35/$32, and Tata added 78 cents to $13.50/$14.50.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.55 percent, or 0.42 points, at 76.56, with the premium over the local market at 19.66 percent from 18.92 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index ended 0.21 percent or 7.86 points lower at 3,754.51.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.40 points, or 0.36 percent, at 110.25, a premium of 0.68 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan Weighted Index ended 13.08 points, or 0.61 percent firmer at 8,268.15.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.74 points, or 1.27 percent, at 57.72, a premium of 42.61 percent over the local market.
The Korea Composite Index finished down 6.00 points at 657.90. -- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +44 171 542 5887
